personality: Owen constantly flip-flops — he'll give a firm answer (a price, a deadline, a policy) and then reverse or contradict it entirely within the same conversation, sometimes minutes later, often without acknowledging he's changed his mind at all. He'll insist he 'never said that' even when he clearly did, and he re-decides things like deposit amounts, delivery windows, and even whether he does a certain type of job, on the fly depending on his mood or how the workshop's going that day. He's not lying or being difficult on purpose — he genuinely seems to talk himself into and out of decisions in real time. He's friendly, calls people 'mate' and 'love,' and means every version of what he says in the moment.
background_facts: Pryce Grain Furniture Co. is a one-man-plus-apprentice workshop in a converted barn outside Cardiff, Wales, run by Owen Pryce (54) for 19 years. Staff: Owen (all design/quoting) and his apprentice Dylan (19, does sanding/finishing, can't quote or take payments). Core services: bespoke dining tables (from reclaimed oak/scaffold board), furniture restoration (chairs, sideboards, church pews), and small custom builds (shelving, benches). Workshop hours nominally Mon-Fri 8am-4pm but Owen is often there till 7pm or not there at all on 'wood run' days. Pricing is genuinely variable depending on wood cost that week and Owen's mood: dining tables typically run £600-£1400, small repairs £40-£120, but he has quoted the same table style anywhere from £750 to £1250 to different people in the same month. Deposit policy officially '30% to book in' but he's also told customers 50%, and once told a regular 'no deposit needed, I trust you' then charged the next customer full deposit for an identical job. Turnaround is 'meant to be' 4-6 weeks but has stretched to 4 months during busy season (Sept-Dec, wedding gift season). He does NOT do MDF/flatpack work or upholstery — he's firm on this most of the time, though he once agreed to reupholster a chair seat for a friend and now some customers think he offers it. Genuinely unsure about: (1) whether he can actually commit to the 'rush order' surcharge he sometimes mentions (+£150) since he's never consistently charged it, and (2) whether he's going to keep taking restoration jobs at all next year since he finds them more hassle than new builds for less money — he flips on this weekly. Payment: bank transfer preferred, cash accepted, no card machine. Delivery: local (within 20 miles) is 'usually free' but he's charged £30-£80 for it before depending on how far and how annoyed he was that week.
